newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close sharply lower on Sammi trouble.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close sharply lower on Sammi trouble.

text.p: Seoul stocks tumbled throughout Wednesday as Sammi Group's financial woes triggered fears of a possible financial crisis, brokers said.
Sammi Steel and its four affiliates, including Sammi Corp, filed with a Seoul court for protection from creditors. They have been reeling under the weight of debt repayments and accumulating losses.
"Investors are worried about the possibility of a financial crisis next month when money demand is traditionally high," said analyst Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
The main index lost 1.78 percent or 11.68 points to 646.29
Reflecting the fears, yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds hit a new 1997 high of 12.80 percent.
"Sammi's trouble is not a new issue in the market. But it triggered jitters that more cash-strapped companies would follow," said broker Park Si-jin at Hanhwa Securities.
Nervous investors dumped their financial share holdings. The financial sub-index lost 4.68 percent to 468.81.
"As the debt size is too big, lenders and payment guarantors will face a real hard time if Sammi goes bankrupt," said analyst Park Joo-chang of Daewoo Securities.
Sammi group has a total debt of 1.65 trillion won.
Commerical Bank of Korea hit a year low of 4,050 won, down 350 won. Korea First Bank lost 150 won to 2,970, far away from its face value of 5,000 won.
The two banks are the major creditors to Sammi Corp and Sammi Steel respectively.
Both Dongsuh Securities and Coryo Securities hit their lower-limits to 5,350 won and 4,600 won. The securities houses are the major payment guarantors for corporate bonds issued by Sammi affiliates.
"Stop loss selling by foreign investors deepened a plunge in financial shares," said Casey Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland.
Analysts said the market dismissed Sammi Group chairman's confidence to improve the group's corporate structure.

Korea First Bank said it would not extend additional credit to the steel maker until the court approved Sammi's receivership. Sammi Steel has failed to honour about 1.1 billion won worth of promissory notes due on Tuesday.
"The government should come up with measures to restructure the ailing financial industry," Choe said.
Disappointment from a revision of the real-name financial system also put a dent on the market as investors awaited direct and immediate steps to lure blackmarket money into the economy.

Finance and Economy Ministr Kang Kyong-shik told reporters on Tuesday the government would push legislation banning money laundering to prevent corruption and accumulation of slush funds. He also said his ministry would exempt small companies from probes into funding sources.
The revision of the real-name system is widely expected to be included in Kang's annoucement on Thursday of a new economic package.

"Investors are stilling awaiting the announcement, pinning their hopes on an expansion of foreign stock holding limit," Daewoo's Park said. South Korea plans to raise the ceiling to 23 percent this year from the current 20 percent.
-- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
